title: Smoke and Mirrors
text: Smoke and Mirrors is about visualising not just the methane data (smoke) in a way people can really absorb but also the disinformation campaign (mirrors) which has caused the data to be denied, doubted and delayed through the decades.
speaker: Beatie Wolfe
source: Statement of Intent, Smoke and Mirrors (beatiewolfe.com)

title: Smoke and Mirrors
text: Realising that a crucial piece of the climate puzzle (how we got to this critical point) has been the fossil fuel industry’s response to the emerging environmental awareness of the 1970s, and that methane emissions (30 times more potent than carbon for trapping heat) are increasingly linked with that industry, I wanted to illuminate this key parallel timeline.
speaker: Beatie Wolfe
source: Statement of Intent, Smoke and Mirrors (beatiewolfe.com)

title: Smoke and Mirrors
text: The ‘smoke and mirrors’ tactics of the big oil industry (and many political bodies and corporations) are so hard to grasp, which leaves a lot of people feeling disempowered, so I wanted this project to help make this slippery reality visible and tangible.
speaker: Beatie Wolfe
source: Hannah Bachl, "From Blue Marble to Bioplastic Record", Ars Electronica Blog, 17 June 2024

title: Smoke and Mirrors
text: It is very important to me that anyone can see the work and immediately get a sense of what they’re viewing
speaker: Beatie Wolfe
source: Hannah Bachl, "From Blue Marble to Bioplastic Record", Ars Electronica Blog, 17 June 2024

title: Smoke and Mirrors
text: In both cases I feel that the music, lyrics etc. really help to bring the data and message to life, to make it feelable and relatable via art’s emotive power.
speaker: Beatie Wolfe
source: Hannah Bachl, "From Blue Marble to Bioplastic Record", Ars Electronica Blog, 17 June 2024

title: Soak
text: Dying fabric is a time-honored tradition of humankind.
speaker: everyware (Yunsil Heo, Hyunwoo Bang)
source: 'Soak, Dye in light.' by everyware (2011), everyware.kr portfolio

title: Soak
text: Especially in Korea, people have deep affection toward the unique colors and textures of fabric dyed with traditional materials.
speaker: everyware (Yunsil Heo, Hyunwoo Bang)
source: 'Soak, Dye in light.' by everyware (2011), everyware.kr portfolio

title: Soak
text: Now in the age of new media, we tried a whole new way of coloring fabrics with the essential materials of new media, ‘light’ and ‘interactivity’.
speaker: everyware (Yunsil Heo, Hyunwoo Bang)
source: 'Soak, Dye in light.' by everyware (2011), everyware.kr portfolio

title: Soak
text: Also, as a meta-creative interactive installation, ‘Soak’ can be expanded for creating garments with personalized patterns or textile productions using today’s digital fabric printing technologies.
speaker: everyware (Yunsil Heo, Hyunwoo Bang)
source: 'Soak, Dye in light.' by everyware (2011), everyware.kr portfolio

title: Soft Collision
text: Soft Collision (2024) looks at the potential of safe physical interaction by embracing collision rather than avoiding it. Creating a tangible interface between humans and robots as a tool for direct manipulation and live programming.
speaker: Anna Schaeffner
source: Artist website, Soft Collision

title: Soft Collision
text: The Soft Collision project subverted this event by exploring it as an alternative means of communication between human and robot.
speaker: Anna Schaeffner
source: Schaeffner, 'Soft Collision', abstract for Drôles d'objets 2025, Lannion (translated from French)

title: Soft Collision
text: Thus, the energy involved in a collision creates a deformation of matter, which itself becomes the interaction.
speaker: Anna Schaeffner
source: Schaeffner, 'Soft Collision', abstract for Drôles d'objets 2025, Lannion (translated from French)

title: Soft Collision
text: The communicative potential of the material calls for other forms of intelligence through body language.
speaker: Anna Schaeffner
source: Schaeffner, 'Soft Collision', abstract for Drôles d'objets 2025, Lannion (translated from French)

title: Solwata
text: The ocean that’s consuming their world is the same ocean that connects us all. We created this mixed reality installation to collapse that distance.
speaker: Felix Gaedtke, Gayatri Parameswaran (NowHere Media)
source: La Biennale di Venezia, Venice Immersive 2026 — Main Creators' Statement (NowHere Media - Felix Gaedtke, Gayatri Parameswaran)

title: Solwata
text: It forces a reckoning: what is your position in this? What will you do when these changes arrive at your door? That’s the question we want audiences to sit with.
speaker: Felix Gaedtke, Gayatri Parameswaran (NowHere Media)
source: La Biennale di Venezia, Venice Immersive 2026 — Main Creators' Statement (NowHere Media - Felix Gaedtke, Gayatri Parameswaran)

title: Solwata
text: One moment from our trip stays with us – diving underwater to see the remains of the submerged island of Walande, which was once home to a thriving community, now entirely displaced due to rising sea levels. It was sobering, and struck us deeply: this could be all our futures.
speaker: Felix Gaedtke, Gayatri Parameswaran (NowHere Media)
source: La Biennale di Venezia, Venice Immersive 2026 — Main Creators' Statement (NowHere Media - Felix Gaedtke, Gayatri Parameswaran)

title: Solwata
text: Climate change can feel overwhelming because it's often discussed in abstract terms. We wanted to make it tangible by showing what it means for individual people and families.
speaker: Felix Gaedtke
source: Climate Week NYC, 'Environmental justice starts with people: How Solwata brings climate displacement into focus' (interview)

title: Solwata
text: Our goal is for these voices to be heard by the people who have the power to act.
speaker: Gayatri Parameswaran
source: Climate Week NYC, 'Environmental justice starts with people: How Solwata brings climate displacement into focus' (interview)

title: SONG 1
text: Song 1 is based on one song, what I think is a very perfect pop song. I wanted to take this one specific song and see if that could become the structure for this artwork, and if that song could be reinterpreted in many different ways and eventually create its own landscape.
speaker: Doug Aitken
source: Daoud Tyler-Ameen, 'Millions Of People Go By: Doug Aitken's "Song 1" Distills City Life', NPR (via KUNC), 20 May 2012, quoting Aitken's press statement

title: SONG 1
text: If we have this phenomenal building that's very monolithic in its form and structure, then can we make it almost liquid architecture?
speaker: Doug Aitken
source: David Sokol, 'Song 1', Architectural Record, 16 May 2012

title: SONG 1
text: There is an invisible rhythm to the way the light moves, the way the edits transpire,
speaker: Doug Aitken
source: David Sokol, 'Song 1', Architectural Record, 16 May 2012

title: SONG 1
text: Can you make architecture that has a certain tempo?
speaker: Doug Aitken
source: Kriston Capps, 'Screen Song', Artforum, 26 March 2012, reporting Aitken's talk with Kerry Brougher at the opening

title: Songs for dying
text: It started out as this research project on animistic and shamanic traditions in different countries and places that were colonised, where you can kind of trace the effects and the built-up trauma.
speaker: Korakrit Arunanondchai
source: The Art Newspaper, 'Korakrit Arunanondchai: on loss, shamanism—and denim' (24 Sept 2021)

title: Songs for dying
text: Most of Songs for dying was shot on the beach where my grandfather raised me in Thailand. When he was cremated, his bones turned to coral, and I went out on a boat and returned them to the sea.
speaker: Korakrit Arunanondchai
source: The Art Newspaper, 'Korakrit Arunanondchai: on loss, shamanism—and denim' (24 Sept 2021)

title: Songs for dying
text: It was hard to tell exactly the moment he died, or what was actually gone. If there was a spirit, when did the spirit leave the body? I was just thinking about shamans using songs as mediums, or even the idea of songs as a method for gathering and transcending to a higher power or this transcendent space.
speaker: Korakrit Arunanondchai
source: The Art Newspaper, 'Korakrit Arunanondchai: on loss, shamanism—and denim' (24 Sept 2021)

title: Songs for dying
text: In Songs for Dying , one of the central ideas is decomposition. I talk about ghosts themselves as decomposers: how they digest ancestral memories, trauma, things that seem like they can’t be processed in one person’s lifetime.
speaker: Korakrit Arunanondchai
source: The White Review, interview with Korakrit Arunanondchai (2021)

title: Songs for dying
text: In Songs for Dying , the membrane becomes the ghost: an embodiment of the space between disparate locations or events where ideas or emotions get translated.
speaker: Korakrit Arunanondchai
source: The White Review, interview with Korakrit Arunanondchai (2021)

title: Sonic Inheritances
artist: Singing Wells (Ketebul Music and Abubilla Music)
text: Our goal is to record, archive and share the traditional music of East Africa for two important reasons – to sustain and celebrate the extraordinary cultural music heritage of the region and to help make this legacy relevant and fresh to today’s audiences.
speaker: Singing Wells
source: Singing Wells, 'Mission'

title: Sonic Inheritances
artist: Singing Wells (Ketebul Music and Abubilla Music)
text: As a group of sound and video engineers, producers and musicians, we set out on this mission not to become ‘fossil collectors’ and store the recordings in inaccessible archives. We work with musicians to make sure their music traditions continue to be practiced, can be shared amongst the widest audiences and become a source of inspiration for new musicians.
speaker: Singing Wells
source: Singing Wells, 'Mission'

title: Sonic Inheritances
artist: Singing Wells (Ketebul Music and Abubilla Music)
text: Singing Wells can’t be just about archiving. We can’t be fossil collectors. We also have to make sure we can bring these traditions into modern music.
speaker: Steve Kivutia, Ketebul Music
source: Singing Wells, 'What We Do'

title: Sonic Inheritances
artist: Singing Wells (Ketebul Music and Abubilla Music)
text: We are committed to supporting traditional music performance in rural East Africa as we believe that this not only serves to promote and preserve the cultural heritage of a community but is also a key indicator of the sustainability of that community.
speaker: Singing Wells
source: Singing Wells, 'What We Do'

title: Soundtrack
text: In ‘Soundtrack,’ the idea was to reverse the usual American film projection — the world as a projection of family drama — into the situation where the world is projected into the family,
speaker: Guy Ben-Ner
source: Alicia Eler, review of Guy Ben-Ner's 'Soundtrack' at Aspect Ratio Gallery, Hyperallergic, 8 April 2013

title: Soundtrack
text: The basic idea has been with me for more than ten years,
speaker: Guy Ben-Ner
source: Alicia Eler, review of Guy Ben-Ner's 'Soundtrack' at Aspect Ratio Gallery, Hyperallergic, 8 April 2013

title: Soundtrack
text: It is the mechanism of the work — budding, or the opposite of dubbing — images to a pre-existing, readymade soundtrack.
speaker: Guy Ben-Ner
source: Alicia Eler, review of Guy Ben-Ner's 'Soundtrack' at Aspect Ratio Gallery, Hyperallergic, 8 April 2013

title: Speak Slowly and It Will Become a Song
text: Before the work for Aichi was decided, I had the chance to hear a lecture by Kim HeyJung, a researcher of Korean folk songs, and I became interested in women's folk songs. Unlike men's, women's folk songs are said to be characterised by carrying the story of one's own life in the song. I thought it was wonderful how narration becomes melody and turns into music, and I wondered what meaning such folk songs have in the present day.
speaker: Kwon Byungjun
source: BRUTUS.jp, 'Korean Cultural News' Vol.22 Artist Kwon Byungjun (translated from Japanese)

title: Speak Slowly and It Will Become a Song
text: I think it is music that still has meaning today, and the spirit and significance that folk songs carry are wonderful, so I want to introduce them to young people.
speaker: Kwon Byungjun
source: BRUTUS.jp, 'Korean Cultural News' Vol.22 Artist Kwon Byungjun (translated from Japanese)

title: Speak Slowly and It Will Become a Song
text: In Seto City, I asked women in their 60s and 70s to improvise songs of their own lives and sing them.
speaker: Kwon Byungjun
source: BRUTUS.jp, 'Korean Cultural News' Vol.22 Artist Kwon Byungjun (translated from Japanese)

title: Speak Slowly and It Will Become a Song
text: At the venue, you put on headphones I made, fitted with an original high-precision GPS antenna, and as you walk across the wide space you can experience more than 360 different soundscapes. You hear songs, starting with folk songs, and narration, and the areas around them are filled with background sounds of the folk songs as interpreted by AI.
speaker: Kwon Byungjun
source: BRUTUS.jp, 'Korean Cultural News' Vol.22 Artist Kwon Byungjun (translated from Japanese)

title: Species series
text: In my work, a series of artificial life forms such as autonomous kinetic objects and robotic creatures are created to have birth, life, and death in varying environments.
speaker: Yang Wonbin
source: Species Series, Simultan festival archive (2014)

title: Species series
text: I investigate how these artificial life forms take the cities as their habitats, utilize urban facilities and systems for their purposes, build interspecific relationships with other beings, and develop survival strategies to live in the man-made surroundings.
speaker: Yang Wonbin
source: Species Series, Simultan festival archive (2014)

title: Species series
text: I trace each creature’s unique histories of emergence, adaptation, and evolution while I observe how people and societies react to these aliens and strangers.
speaker: Yang Wonbin
source: Species Series, Simultan festival archive (2014)

title: Species series
text: The different levels of technological complexities reflect the evolutionary histories of the robotic species.
speaker: Yang Wonbin
source: Artist Statement, Wonbin Yang: Species Series, SIGGRAPH Asia 2012: Echo (ACM SIGGRAPH Art Archive)

title: Species series
text: Relatively advanced technologies are gradually merged into their next generations as a result of struggles for existence and survival.
speaker: Yang Wonbin
source: Artist Statement, Wonbin Yang: Species Series, SIGGRAPH Asia 2012: Echo (ACM SIGGRAPH Art Archive)

title: Sports Time Machine
text: What the Machine does is to preserve and store the experience as a medium and share it with others in future, unlike one’s memory never to be retrieved.
speaker: Hiroshi Inukai / Sports Time Machine project
source: 'English Video has Released', post by Hakase Inukai, Sports Time Machine project blog (19 March 2014)

title: Sports Time Machine
text: With the Machine, you experience physical communications that intersect past, present, and future through sports.
speaker: Hiroshi Inukai / Sports Time Machine project
source: 'English Video has Released', post by Hakase Inukai, Sports Time Machine project blog (19 March 2014)

title: Sports Time Machine
text: While being shared in local communities, the Machine is simultaneously developed, maintained, and revised by reflecting how it is being played with.
speaker: Hiroshi Inukai / Sports Time Machine project
source: 'English Video has Released', post by Hakase Inukai, Sports Time Machine project blog (19 March 2014)

title: Sports Time Machine
text: We believe that this openness to its function is distinctively similar to what conventional sports did to our societies, and this is one way how a future sports will contribute to the communities.
speaker: Hiroshi Inukai / Sports Time Machine project
source: 'English Video has Released', post by Hakase Inukai, Sports Time Machine project blog (19 March 2014)

title: Spray and Pray
text: It examines how digital media infrastructures produce belief, working through a speculative documentary form that reconstructs automated news networks and algorithmic content systems. Rather than documenting single events, the film stages the mechanisms through which credibility is manufactured.
speaker: Veneta Androva
source: ArtReview, Venice Biennale: Artist Q&As (Bulgaria), 28 May 2026

title: Spray and Pray
text: Spray and Pray works within these ‘minor’ zones – the background infrastructures, automated protocols and algorithmically amplified signals that shape collective imagination. Rather than focusing on visible events, the film examines the conditions that make certain narratives persuasive.
speaker: Veneta Androva
source: ArtReview, Venice Biennale: Artist Q&As (Bulgaria), 28 May 2026

title: Spray and Pray
text: The film treats their outputs not as evidence, but as unstable readings, surfaces that expose the limits, biases, and ambiguities of automated interpretation.
speaker: Veneta Androva
source: Spray and Pray, work page, venetaandrova.com

title: Spray and Pray
text: The tension between raw documentary trace and reconstructed mediation mirrors the very conditions the film investigates: an informational environment in which authenticity is perpetually produced, circulated, and destabilized.
speaker: Veneta Androva
source: Spray and Pray, work page, venetaandrova.com

title: Spray and Pray
text: In Spray and Pray, speculation becomes a form of evidence, tracing opaque infrastructures in which agency, authorship, and responsibility are continuously displaced.
speaker: Veneta Androva
source: Catalogue text, Prix Ars Electronica Archive 2026

title: SQUEEEQUE-SPEAKERDOME
text: It’s a project that I proposed as a performance space for strangers to get involved in collaborative song
speaker: Alexis O'Hara
source: Emily Raine, "Squeeeeque!: Alexis O'Hara's sonic igloo", Cult MTL, 28 November 2012

title: SQUEEEQUE-SPEAKERDOME
text: I’ve wired about 34 of the speakers, and when people go into the igloo, there are microphones hanging from the ceiling, and they can grab the mic and talk into it and the voices go through a delay and a phaser and then coming out of the walls of the speakerbox igloo.
speaker: Alexis O'Hara
source: Emily Raine, "Squeeeeque!: Alexis O'Hara's sonic igloo", Cult MTL, 28 November 2012

title: SQUEEEQUE-SPEAKERDOME
text: An immersive environment, cosy as a children’s fort, built from items discarded by society. A sonic cocoon woven from the mutations of your own voice, reverberating across walls and ceiling.
speaker: Alexis O'Hara
source: SQUEEEEQUE – SPEAKERDOME, project page on the artist's site (dyslex6.com)

title: SQUEEEQUE-SPEAKERDOME
text: As I am a settler on unceded indigenous territory and have no blood connection to the Inuit, I acknowledge that to use the word “igloo” to describe or name an artwork of my making is appropriative and frankly racist.
speaker: Alexis O'Hara
source: "A long overdue acknowledgement of cultural appropriation", artist's site, 23 April 2021

title: SQUEEEQUE-SPEAKERDOME
text: Full of questions and forever a clown, I am attracted to distortions, larsens, feedback and artifice. I spend a lot of time thinking about the utility of art.
speaker: Alexis O'Hara
source: Artist statement, About page, artist's site (dyslex6.com)

title: Stained
text: The film takes place in the narrative world of Mojo, a fictional future I created as a way of bridging the disparities between the contemporary Black experience and landscape discourse. It is a response to my experience in landscape architecture where we were taught to see, study, and interpret landscapes from a limited point of view.
speaker: Jeremy Kamal
source: Ars Electronica Archive — Stained (Prix Ars Electronica 2024)

title: Stained
text: It embraces the friction and harmony that emerges when green agendas (climate activism, environmentalism, ecological study) and contemporary Black experience collide. In their collision, I mine for new rituals, mythologies, and landscapes that challenge our conventional understanding of "nature" and space.
speaker: Jeremy Kamal
source: Ars Electronica Archive — Stained (Prix Ars Electronica 2024)

title: Stained
text: A reason why I took the topic of gang culture is because I particularly did not want to stray away from all aspects of what we deal with in Black life,
speaker: Jeremy Kamal
source: UCSB HFA — Mojo: When Black Identity Shapes the Earth (talk report, 2023)

title: Stained
text: There are opportunities to redefine and reframe these things in a new context, that can take them out of these narratives that we see them through today, and look at them as opportunities for the future.
speaker: Jeremy Kamal
source: UCSB HFA — Mojo: When Black Identity Shapes the Earth (talk report, 2023)

title: Stained
text: Often when we talk about Blackness, the conversation orbits around political systems and social systems, but never around natural ones.
speaker: Jeremy Kamal
source: UCSB HFA — Mojo: When Black Identity Shapes the Earth (talk report, 2023)

title: Still Life: Icon and Fetish (manifestation 1)
text: Positing the question, can machines be taught aesthetics, here the artist trains a machine to look at thousands of still-life paintings, some in their entirety, and some in their details, to try and guide a machine to learn both composition and the painterly nuances of aesthetic.
speaker: Harshit Agrawal
source: (Un)Still Life- Icon and Fetish, artist's website

title: Still Life: Icon and Fetish (manifestation 1)
text: In any painting what is the relation of the part (as fetish) to the whole (as icon)? How can one teach a computer compositional structure and painterly texture? This work tries to start poking into these set of questions.
speaker: Harshit Agrawal
source: (Un)Still Life- Icon and Fetish, artist's website (archival print on canvas)

title: Still Life: Icon and Fetish (manifestation 1)
text: For the second AI, the learning rate is kept fast since the attempt is for the machine to learn abstracted visuals from the dataset - the painterly as opposed to the compositional of the first. Thus, experimenting with both treatments of the dataset and the AI learning process, a new study in aesthetics of icon and fetish emerges.
speaker: Harshit Agrawal
source: STIR, 'Harshit Agrawal's Exo-stential is India's first solo artificial intelligence art show' (interview by Rahul Kumar), 5 October 2021

title: Still Life: Icon and Fetish (manifestation 1)
text: Beyond the conceptual, I am interested in exploring the evolution of aesthetics too enabled by the process of teaching machines a visual language from given examples and varying the training process to produce different visual outcomes, like in Still Life: Icon and Fetish .
speaker: Harshit Agrawal
source: STIR, 'Harshit Agrawal's Exo-stential is India's first solo artificial intelligence art show' (interview by Rahul Kumar), 5 October 2021

title: Still Life: Icon and Fetish (manifestation 1)
text: Having said that, what is fascinating with AI art for the human artist to engage with is - even when machines look at human-labelled human-curated objects (datasets), the generalisations they form (or the patterns they learn from it) are profoundly alien.
speaker: Harshit Agrawal
source: STIR, 'Harshit Agrawal's Exo-stential is India's first solo artificial intelligence art show' (interview by Rahul Kumar), 5 October 2021

title: Stories from the Earth
text: My practice is one of storytelling. It's about the message rather than just the materiality of the work.
speaker: Helena Uambembe
source: PAPER – in conversation with Helena Uambembe 2024/2025 (Nisha Merit)

title: Stories from the Earth
text: So my practice is me looking at how global history and politics are personal and domestic, because that's how I came to exist and how my community came to Pomfret which is connected to global history and politics
speaker: Helena Uambembe
source: PAPER – in conversation with Helena Uambembe 2024/2025 (Nisha Merit)

title: Stories from the Earth
text: And in order for it not to sit and drive me crazy, I had to find ways around it. I was lucky to have worked with Teresa Kutala Fermino [Johannesburg based multimedia artists, who grew up in Pomfret during the same time] and we found ways to deal with that together through writing fairy tales. And from there I continued to write stories but I made them fun.
speaker: Helena Uambembe
source: PAPER – in conversation with Helena Uambembe 2024/2025 (Nisha Merit)

title: Stories from the Earth
text: There was a time I described myself as a storykeeper because I have these archives I would love to make accessible to my community.
speaker: Helena Uambembe
source: PAPER – in conversation with Helena Uambembe 2024/2025 (Nisha Merit)

title: Stranger Visions
text: Working with the traces strangers unwittingly left behind, the project was meant to call attention to the developing technology of forensic DNA phenotyping, the potential for a culture of biological surveillance, and the impulse towards genetic determinism.
speaker: Heather Dewey-Hagborg (artist's website)
source: Stranger Visions, project page, deweyhagborg.com

title: Stranger Visions
text: Since this time I have devoted critical efforts to discussing the limitations and bias in phenotyping technology, which I (and many scientists) do not consider accurate or impartial enough for use in criminal investigations.
speaker: Heather Dewey-Hagborg (artist's website)
source: Stranger Visions, project page, deweyhagborg.com

title: Stranger Visions
text: I just became obsessed with thinking about whose hair that was, and what they might look like, and what they might be like,
speaker: Heather Dewey-Hagborg
source: Acacia Squires, 'Litterbugs Beware: Turning Found DNA Into Portraits', NPR, 12 May 2013

title: Stranger Visions
text: This person is more likely to be overweight, to have pale skin, to have freckles, blue eyes, how do I interpret this?
speaker: Heather Dewey-Hagborg
source: Acacia Squires, 'Litterbugs Beware: Turning Found DNA Into Portraits', NPR, 12 May 2013

title: Study for Strings
text: Like in Kassel, for instance, it was the atmosphere of the train station that drew me. “Study for Strings” started from standing at the platform's end and thinking about sound coming from a distance.
speaker: Susan Philipsz
source: Art21, 'Susan Philipsz in "Berlin"', Art in the Twenty-First Century, Season 9 (2018), English subtitles (Amara)

title: Study for Strings
text: In the original composition, it was a 24-piece orchestra. What I decided to do was to record just two of the parts. Silence really makes you think about the absence of the other performers who would've been killed.
speaker: Susan Philipsz
source: Art21, 'Susan Philipsz in "Berlin"', Art in the Twenty-First Century, Season 9 (2018), English subtitles (Amara)

title: Study for Strings
text: Train stations, they're very evocative places, places of departure and separation.
speaker: Susan Philipsz
source: Art21, 'Susan Philipsz in "Berlin"', Art in the Twenty-First Century, Season 9 (2018), English subtitles (Amara)

title: Study for Strings
text: I'm interested in the emotive and psychological effects of sound. Often I'm just looking for a place that has an interesting acoustic or architecture history.
speaker: Susan Philipsz
source: Art21, 'Susan Philipsz in "Berlin"', Art in the Twenty-First Century, Season 9 (2018), English subtitles (Amara)

title: Study for Strings
text: But when I do works in public space it is often about the place and activating the acoustics, the architecture and heightening your own sense of self in a particular place.
speaker: Susan Philipsz
source: Louisiana Channel, 'Susan Philipsz: Song As A Trigger Of Memory' (video page text)

title: Subnormal Europe
text: Quoting the text of the agreement between the parties, “the main purpose of this initiative is the exact technical reproduction of those instants, which have marked our history of progress in the audiovisual field. The collection must be composed by a set of files, which may be exhibited together with their originals, not being able to distinguish one from the other.”
speaker: Óscar Escudero & Belenish Moreno-Gil (project text)
source: Catalogue text, Prix Ars Electronica 2021 archive

title: Subnormal Europe
text: The team, in cooperation with the Zentrum für Kunst und Medien Karlsruhe, will face the challenge of creating live replicas of these fragments in each of the performances.
speaker: Óscar Escudero & Belenish Moreno-Gil (project text)
source: Catalogue text, Prix Ars Electronica 2021 archive

title: Subnormal Europe
text: The outcomes of the process will be eventually compiled and stored by the EU in order to fulfill the goals of the project, among them, and quoting again the award agreement: “to take the pulse of the current state of the European values and to reaffirm the sense of citizenship of its inhabitants, as well as the knowledge of our common history and its contributions to human development in difficult times for Europeanism.”
speaker: Óscar Escudero & Belenish Moreno-Gil (project text)
source: Catalogue text, Prix Ars Electronica 2021 archive

title: Subnormal Europe
text: Óscar Escudero & Belenish Moreno-Gil (ES) are a couple of transmedia composers and performers whose productions point on social networks as ideology and the creation of operative artistic devices within a “SPAM reality.”
speaker: Óscar Escudero & Belenish Moreno-Gil (biography)
source: Biography, Prix Ars Electronica 2021 archive

title: Sunshine Monument
text: This is an interesting time to be a digital artist. I feel myself bordering multiple dystopias and utopias simultaneously – some of them are technological, some of them are biological, and some of them are social.
speaker: Peter Burr
source: 150 Media Stream, 'Interview with Peter Burr' (on THE CONTINUOUS MONUMENT)

title: Sunshine Monument
text: As an artist, my job is to put form to those borders and potentially conjure something that is present but invisible otherwise.
speaker: Peter Burr
source: 150 Media Stream, 'Interview with Peter Burr' (on THE CONTINUOUS MONUMENT)

title: Sunshine Monument
text: In choosing this technical path, I also leaned into the ambient nature of the space and built an artwork that can run infinitely without repetition.
speaker: Peter Burr
source: 150 Media Stream, 'Interview with Peter Burr' (on THE CONTINUOUS MONUMENT)

title: System's Void
text: It was more of a conceptual idea to record the Earth and shift the perspective away from the human. I wanted to explore what the Earth “hears” when a pipe goes through it or when a well is constantly pumping and extracting gas.
speaker: Sung Tieu

title: The Glamorous Boys of Tang (1985, Chui Kang-Chien)

title: Wisdoms for Love 3.0
artist: Keiken (with Obso1337, Ryan Vautier, Sakeema Crook)
text: The game explores the bubbled-up feelings, collective consciousness and fervent beliefs of the contemporary moment, where the desire for change and a more equal, decentralised future is collectively being challenged. The game is rooted in decision-making where you must decide your fate, do you take the path of the Divine Mother, become a Human God or stay on your Moral High Horse?
speaker: Keiken
source: Wisdoms for Love 3.0 (Trimester 2) — keiken.cloud

title: Wisdoms for Love 3.0
artist: Keiken (with Obso1337, Ryan Vautier, Sakeema Crook)
text: Wisdoms for Love 3.0 explores and maps out different feelings and beliefs in the contemporary consciousness. It considers ‘wisdom’ as a tool for growth and change and proposes it as a form of currency to transact with that could be applied to the blockchain and integrated into future Web 3.0 technologies, creating alternative definitions of wealth for the ‘life’ game.
speaker: Keiken
source: Wisdoms for Love 3.0 (Trimester 2) — keiken.cloud

title: Wisdoms for Love 3.0

title: Wisdoms for Love 3.0
artist: Keiken (with Obso1337, Ryan Vautier, Sakeema Crook)
text: This piece asks: What wisdom do we need to get to Love 3.0 not just Web 3.0? What kind of decentralized systems do we want in our base reality (the Earth), and the metaverse? And how do we access global kin-making for the future of humanity?
speaker: Keiken
source: Statement, Wisdoms for Love 3.0, Gray Area Festival 2021 (New Art City catalog)

title: Wisdoms for Love 3.0
artist: Keiken (with Obso1337, Ryan Vautier, Sakeema Crook)
text: We often say that we “Reflect on the contemporary as though the now is history.” That means looking at current issues, whether they are political or economic, has to do with climate change, etcetera, and dissecting them and creating this bird’s eye perspective where we reconstruct and build speculative narratives around them.
speaker: Keiken
source: "Keiken: Deconstructing the Now", ArtConnect Magazine (interview)

title: With the Heart Coming Out of the Mouth (Com o coração saindo pela boca)

title: With the Heart Coming Out of the Mouth (Com o coração saindo pela boca)
text: I start from the language as a resource to talk about the strength of a collective feeling, as an allegory that uses the nonsense literality of these images to describe feelings that are difficult to translate, and that carry parallels with what we live in the present
speaker: Jonathas de Andrade
source: ArtReview — 'An Anatomy Fair'

title: With the Heart Coming Out of the Mouth (Com o coração saindo pela boca)

title: Without Us

title: Without Us
text: The responsibility must not be with the individual when we’re suffering from decisions by global corporations aiming to get rich quick.
speaker: Daniel Brandt
source: Album announcement (Erased Tapes press text), Click Roll Boom

title: Without Us
text: I began writing this album in California in 2020. At the time, it was already meant to be a reflection about the slow, relentless disaster of the climate crisis.

source: Album announcement (Erased Tapes press text), Click Roll Boom

title: Without Us
text: For PNK, I recorded the ambient hum of Europe’s largest mall — a symphony of overconsumption, the endless current of goods and distractions.

title: Without Us
text: I don't believe Gaia's epiphany, that we are the problem and the solution is to stop existing, is true. Human beings are part of nature, and we shouldn't see ourselves as something disconnected from it. The idea of the film is to take it to the extreme to show that we are part of the problem, so we need a radical change.
speaker: Daniel Brandt
source: Sopitas, feature with Daniel Brandt on the Without Us film (translated from Spanish)

title: Written To Not Remain
text: Some of the works that I’ve made in the last few years – such as Written to not remain and Teneri Ara Assensu / The sahara is not a hotel – were instantaneous. It was a matter of, “I can’t let go of this”. There’s an urgency around it.
speaker: Tewa Barnosa
source: Canvas (Canvas 117: The Maghreb Issue), interview with Tewa Barnosa

title: Written To Not Remain
text: To look away and make apolitical and abstracted work did not correspond to the reality that people were living, and on both personal and artistic levels there was this urgency to create infrastructures, open up conversations and examine histories.

title: Written To Not Remain
text: Written To Not Remain (12’30) is based on a visual investigation looking into the acts of writing on the walls across post-revolution Libya. positioning collective statements as ephemeral evidence of contemporary and historical dialogue, social commentary, war correspondences, or often silent protests.

title: ÑUQA KAUSAKUSAQ QHEPAYKITAPAS / I WILL OUTLIVE YOU
text: My interest in preexisting images of that political imaginary comes from stories, in how we've been told stories and taught history through imagery. The little gaps between what we know about them and what we believe from them, give us opportunities to reflect on and speculate about the real meaning of images, which we could never fully grasp.
speaker: Claudia Martínez Garay
source: Statement 2019 (transcription of the statement for the 21st Biennial), Videobrasil archive

title: ÑUQA KAUSAKUSAQ QHEPAYKITAPAS / I WILL OUTLIVE YOU
text: So this unknown part of my identity, as an indigenous-looking person, has made me think about Indianism, cultural alienation, colonialism and modernity, making me wonder and encouraging my practice, in which I propose decolonializing ideas and aesthetics, constantly questioning myself whether that is possible or not.
speaker: Claudia Martínez Garay
source: Statement 2019 (transcription of the statement for the 21st Biennial), Videobrasil archive

title: ÑUQA KAUSAKUSAQ QHEPAYKITAPAS / I WILL OUTLIVE YOU
text: The spread-out ceramics in the installation works as remainders and hints of the past, incomplete and apart, just like in the forms of display and the colonial memory present in the glass enclosures in ethnographic museums.
speaker: Claudia Martínez Garay
source: Statement 2019 (transcription of the statement for the 21st Biennial), Videobrasil archive
